title: Workload lockstep causing warmup thrash and token throughput regression
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Summary: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported a sudden ~2-5x increase in TTFT and a 30-60% drop in tokens/sec for short interactive sessions. Root cause is a coordinated warmup and KV-cache rebalancer interaction that causes many sessions to warm simultaneously (lockstep), triggering transient KV span eviction and a warmup credit exhaustion loop.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy model variant mix-quant-8bit and quant-16 on a multiplexed worker pool with default warmup credits
2) Replay short-session workload (median request length 12 tokens) at a burst rate that mimics PLG onboarding (50-200 concurrent small sessions)
3) Observe initial TTFT spike at cluster-level and see KV-prefetch and eviction logs indicating span overlap and repeated warmup retries
4) Metrics: tokens/sec drops, first_token_latency increases, kv_cache_miss_rate spikes, warmup_credit_utilization approaches zero
root_cause_analysis: The rebalancer aggressively consolidates active context spans onto fewer workers to improve cache utility. Under small-session burst traffic the rebalancer and the warmup allocator interact: rebalancer moves spans while warmup is still allocating KV cache, causing redundant prefetches and premature eviction of recently primed spans. The batcher window and kernel selection heuristics then pick a less optimal kernel for short sequences after eviction, amplifying TTFT. An additional contributor: warmup credit bookkeeping did not account for canceled requests, so credits leaked and were not recycled promptly during churn.
mitigation_and_hotfixes_applied: 1) Rollback: Disabled rebalancer move-to-consolidate heuristic in hosted and dedicated pools at 2026-03-02 03:10UTC (temporary safe-mode)
2) Patch: Introduced immediate recycling of warmup credits when requests cancel, and a 250ms debounce before evicting a freshly-populated KV span
3) Tuned batcher to prefer short-seq kernel when median sequence length < 32 for next 48h window
4) Applied targeted config to Private customers: exposed knob allow_rebalancer=false and recommended deferring automated rebalancing during onboarding bursts
rollout_plan: Canary the warmup-credit-recycle patch to 5% of hosted traffic in region us-west1 for 30 minutes, monitor first_token_latency, tokens/sec, kv_cache_hit_ratio, and warmup_credit_pool. If stable, expand to dedicated pools and then apply config to private customers via agentless upgrade flow. If regressions appear, toggle allow_rebalancer=false to mitigate.

2026-03-04 09:15UTC: Follow-up with private customer ops with instructions to set allow_rebalancer=false; provided pre-built config patch
next_steps: 1) Complete canary and promote hotfix to runtime-1.20.1 by 2026-03-12 if no adverse signals
2) Add deterministic test to CI that simulates high churning short-session bursts and validates warmup-credit accounting
3) Revisit rebalancer heuristics to add congestion-awareness and a span-protection window (spec and design doc due 2026-03-19)
4) Postmortem draft and customer RCA to be completed by 2026-03-16
